title: Comparison of Femtosecond Laser-Assisted Cataract Surgery and Conventional Phacoemulsification in Shallow Anterior Chambers and Glaucoma

indication: Symptomatic cataract with shallow anterior chamber (ACD below 2.4 mm per Methods) and elevated IOP (glaucoma); subluxated lens/zonulysis in 26 of 106 eyes (10 FLACS, 16 conventional); one eye per patient

groups.description: Femtosecond laser-assisted cataract surgery (LenSx capsulotomy and lens fragmentation) then phaco-chop phacoemulsification and SN60WF IOL
Conventional phacoemulsification (keratome incisions, manual capsulorhexis, phaco-chop) with the same IOL

series.baseline_label: Preoperation = preoperative ECD of the operated eye (EM-3000 specular microscope, Methods 2.4)
series.notes: mean ± SD (tab3 footnote); per-visit n not reported; n = group size from Results

exclusions.reason: loss derived from the same series; the absolute ECD series is used

notes: Retrospective single-centre review (2016-2018); patients chose the procedure after counselling; same surgeon, same phaco platform and IOL.

Role assignment: FLACS and conventional phacoemulsification are two established techniques compared in a retrospective observational design, with no investigational agent and no arm declared experimental, so both are control (separate groups).
ECD was measured preoperatively and at 3 and 6 months (Methods 2.4).
Methods give the shallow-AC inclusion criterion as ACD below 2.4 mm, the Discussion as below 2.5 mm.
